assessment.independence: NOT independent: the same AI system family wrote the code under review. This assessment cannot discharge GATE-016 1_security_review or DEF-026.
assessment.environment: dev container; hosted form run from a copy of the released tree on 127.0.0.1:4011 with a throwaway PostgreSQL 17.11 database; local form run from a scratch copy on 127.0.0.1:4101-4102

findings.title: A planted key entry makes an honest save hand balance readings and new history entries to a member who edited the vault file
findings.affected_households_scope: one member attacks the others in their own household
attack_prerequisites: T1: a member who can edit the vault file (the stated primary adversary)
the victim makes any later save
findings.impact: An honest save treats a reader with any entry in the item's keys map as legitimate and seals fresh reading and ledger keys to them. The integrity banner shows nothing, or clears after the save.
findings.financial_harm: Disclosure only; no money movement exists.
findings.privacy_harm: Another member's balances, debts and their history, in the financial-control setting PRI-002 exists for.
findings.reproduction: Released lib (diff -rq identical); f01_attacks.exs scenarios B, C, C2: attacker decrypts latest and past readings and a new ledger entry; integrity issues [] after the victim's save.
findings.remediation: Extend keys only to readers whose existing seal the session can verify is of the same key (e.g. HMAC(item_key, recipient) stored with each seal); otherwise never to baseline readers. Longer term, SELF-REVIEW option (a), a signed operation log.
findings.regression_test: Planted-key grantee and owner cases in tamper_test.exs: attacker opens no reading or entry key; integrity issues non-empty.

findings.title: Stored bytes are decoded with binary_to_term [:safe], which still accepts function terms, and the decoded vault is not shape-checked
affected_data: the server process and every unlocked session's keys
findings.affected_households_scope: local: the household on the device; hosted: only an attacker who can already write the database
attack_prerequisites: local: T1 can edit the vault file
hosted: database write access
findings.impact: A function value from the file reached application code and was invoked in a same-VM test. Whether an attacker can turn this into code execution in the real server was not established.
findings.privacy_harm: Potentially every unlocked member's data.
findings.reproduction: fun_check.exs: [:safe] decode returned a function; Plug.Crypto.non_executable_binary_to_term/2 refused the same bytes.
findings.remediation: Decode with Plug.Crypto.non_executable_binary_to_term(bin, [:safe]) (or a fixed binary framing), then validate the whole vault or row against a strict schema before use.
findings.regression_test: A vault or row containing a function term is refused before any use.

findings.title: A recovery key never expires, cannot be replaced, and still works after the owner changes their passphrase
findings.affected_households_scope: any member whose recovery key someone else has seen
attack_prerequisites: the victim's email address and recovery key (shown once at sign-up; often written down at home)
findings.impact: Complete, repeatable account takeover. The owner is signed out and cannot revoke the old key.
findings.privacy_harm: Full financial profile of the member, repeatedly.
findings.reproduction: Sign up (keep key), change passphrase, POST /recover with the old key and a new passphrase: 200; sign-in with it: 200; owner's session: 302 to sign-in.
findings.remediation: Let a signed-in member replace the recovery key (re-wrap under a new key, re-authenticated); replace it after every recovery; offer it on passphrase change; tell the member at next sign-in that a recovery happened.
findings.regression_test: After replacement or recovery, the previous key is refused.

findings.title: Item content and history entries can be forged by anyone holding only public keys
affected_data: items and history as shown to members
attack_prerequisites: T1 can edit the vault file
findings.impact: A forged item ('Transfer to Cy (agreed)', owned by Ana) and a forged 'Ana granted Ben' entry appear as genuine; no banner.
findings.financial_harm: Misleading records could support coercion; no money movement.
findings.privacy_harm: Integrity of the member's own record.
findings.reproduction: f01_attacks.exs scenario D; forge_web.exs over HTTP: forged item listed as 'Owned by you'.
findings.remediation: Sign content, entries and readings with the actor's pinned signing key and verify on build (SELF-REVIEW option (a)). Correct DESIGN.md: associated data prevents moving boxes, not forging them.
findings.regression_test: A forged item or entry is rejected or reported.

findings.title: Crashes write decrypted household data, and a malformed sign-in the typed passphrase, to the console log
attack_prerequisites: a crash; shown with self-crafted requests; not shown to be triggerable by T1 against another member
findings.impact: Breaks G5 (no plaintext except by the user's choice) for any crash, including future honest-input bugs.
findings.privacy_harm: Decrypted notes/amounts and a passphrase in terminal output on a shared device.
findings.reproduction: label[]=x to /act/add_value logs the Household with 'Therapy copay SECRETNOTE'; /login without member logs the passphrase.
findings.remediation: Type-guard every parameter; an error handler that logs a reason code only; rescue in Store.handle_call; Inspect with except: for session structs; limit crash-report inspection.
findings.regression_test: List/map parameters on every action give 4xx and the captured log holds no plaintext or passphrase.

findings.title: Anyone who knows a member's address can keep them locked out, and sign-up reveals which addresses have accounts
affected_components: hosted/lib/findependence_hosted/limits.ex (10 failures per address per 15 min)
affected_data: access to the member's own record
attack_prerequisites: the victim's email address
findings.impact: 10 wrong passphrases lock the real owner out for 15 minutes, repeatable indefinitely. Sign-up (unlimited) confirms which addresses are registered.
findings.privacy_harm: Confirms a person uses the service.
findings.reproduction: 10 failed sign-ins for victim@example.com, then the victim's correct passphrase: 401 'Too many attempts'. Sign-up with a taken address: 422 'An account already uses that address.'
findings.remediation: Throttle rather than lock (progressive delay per address+client), exempt the correct passphrase from a client-independent lock, or add a second factor; limit sign-up per client and answer taken addresses the same as new ones.
findings.regression_test: After 10 failures from another client, the owner's correct sign-in succeeds (or is only delayed).

findings.title: One invitation code admits several people when redeemed concurrently
affected_components: hosted/lib/findependence_hosted/tenancy.ex:137-214 (usable/1 locks outside the transaction; used_at set unconditionally)
attack_prerequisites: possession of a valid code; several accounts redeeming within milliseconds
findings.impact: The single-use property fails; extra members join (they gain membership and metadata, not item access).
findings.privacy_harm: Extra members see display names and ownership structure.
findings.reproduction: race.py: 4 concurrent joins per code; 3 of 6 trials admitted more than one account (up to 3).
findings.remediation: Claim the code inside the transaction with UPDATE invitations SET used_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND used_at IS NULL AND withdrawn_at IS NULL AND expires_at>now(), requiring exactly one row.
findings.regression_test: Concurrent joins with one code: exactly one membership.

findings.title: A leftover consent row stops a member who owns nothing from leaving or deleting their account
findings.affected_households_scope: any member who consented to a co-owner's pending proposal
attack_prerequisites: the member once agreed to another member's proposal that is still pending
findings.impact: POST /leave fails with 500; the member stays in the household and cannot delete the account. Only the other owners can clear it.
findings.privacy_harm: Undermines exit (CAP-002, PRI-003) in exactly the coercive setting the product targets.
findings.reproduction: leave.py: 3 co-owners; B proposes owners={B}; A agrees; A relinquishes; A leaves: 500, foreign_key_violation proposal_members_member; still a member.
findings.remediation: Remove the leaver from every proposal's consents in Exit.leave; delete the departed member's proposal_members rows before the membership (or ON DELETE CASCADE).
findings.regression_test: The scenario ends with the member gone and the proposal pending with the remaining consents.

findings.title: Attempt limits are keyed on the connection's address, so behind the required reverse proxy every visitor shares one counter
affected_data: sign-in, recovery and joining for everyone
attack_prerequisites: deployment behind a proxy (the listener is loopback-only)
findings.impact: 30 failures from anyone refuse sign-in, recovery and joining for everyone for 15 minutes.
findings.privacy_harm: None.
findings.reproduction: Not run as a proxy deployment; the listener binds 127.0.0.1 and no forwarded-address handling exists.
findings.remediation: Take the client from a trusted proxy's X-Forwarded-For only (RemoteIp limited to the proxy), in the deploying WorkItem.
findings.regression_test: Two forwarded addresses behind a trusted peer count separately; a spoofed header from an untrusted peer is ignored.

findings.title: Every page loads and decodes the whole household, and nothing bounds a household's size
affected_components: no per-household item cap; bring-in adds up to 2,000 items per request
affected_data: service for the household and CPU for the node
findings.affected_households_scope: the member's household; the node's other households share CPU
attack_prerequisites: a member of the household
findings.impact: GET / grew from 6 ms to 499 ms between 0 and 2,000 items, faster than linear.
findings.privacy_harm: None.
findings.reproduction: Adding items in one household: 0 → 6 ms, 250 → 30 ms, 1,000 → 106 ms, 2,000 → 499 ms for GET /.
findings.remediation: A per-household and per-member item cap; per-member write rate limits; load only the member's readable rows plus structure; profile the superlinear step.
findings.regression_test: Adding past the cap is refused; page time at the cap stays under a budget.

findings.title: The relinquish confirmation names the owners of an item the member cannot see
affected_data: ownership of hidden items; whether an item id exists
attack_prerequisites: a member who knows a hidden item's id
findings.impact: 'LB and LD will keep it.' for a hidden item versus 'No one will keep it.' for a missing id.
findings.privacy_harm: Metadata already plaintext by design (ASM-020), but it contradicts co_owners' own documentation and REQ-102.
findings.reproduction: POST /confirm/relinquish item=<hidden id> as a non-reader.
findings.remediation: Require the item to be visible and owned by the member; otherwise the not-found page.
findings.regression_test: A hidden id and a random id give identical 404 bodies.

findings.title: Refusals from pages other than home, and unexpected parameter shapes, crash with 500
attack_prerequisites: a signed-in member
findings.impact: A refused item action whose return path is not a visible item page shows a 500 instead of its message; list/map parameters give 500s. No state changed in any case tested.
findings.privacy_harm: None in production (no debug page).
findings.reproduction: POST /act/delete item=<not yours> without return: 500 'no "home" html template defined for ActionHTML'.
findings.remediation: put_view(HomeHTML) in render_home; guard parameter types (is_binary) at decoding.
findings.regression_test: Every /act action refused without a return renders home with 422; shape fuzzing gives no 500.

findings.title: Production database settings: no TLS, one owner role for migrations and runtime, audit table writable
findings.form: hosted (deployment-dependent; MEDIUM if the database is off-host)
affected_data: wrapped keys, ciphertext, display names, audit records in transit
attack_prerequisites: network position between app and database, or an application compromise
findings.impact: Unencrypted database traffic; a compromise can alter schema and rewrite audit records.
findings.privacy_harm: Metadata and ciphertext exposure in transit.
findings.reproduction: Config reading; dev server ssl=off, single superuser role.
findings.remediation: ssl with verify_peer; a DML-only runtime role separate from the migration owner; REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE on audit_events.
findings.regression_test: A config test asserts verified TLS; a deployment check lists the runtime role's privileges.

findings.title: Hosted signed-in pages and the export download may be kept in the browser cache
attack_prerequisites: later access to the same browser profile
findings.impact: cache-control is 'max-age=0, private, must-revalidate', not no-store.
findings.privacy_harm: Decrypted financial pages persisting on a shared device after sign-out.
findings.reproduction: GET / and /export.json response headers.
findings.remediation: cache-control: no-store in the signed-in pipeline and on export_json.
findings.regression_test: ConnTest asserts no-store on /, /items/:id, /export.json.

findings.title: Local flash messages carrying item names travel in a signed but unencrypted cookie
attack_prerequisites: access to the browser's cookie store
findings.impact: 'Added “Therapy copay …”.' readable in the cookie until the next page.
findings.privacy_harm: Item names in browser storage on disk.
findings.reproduction: Decode the session cookie after adding an item.
findings.remediation: encryption_salt, or keep flash server-side.
findings.regression_test: No user text in the cookie payload.

findings.title: Local 421 and 500 responses lack the security headers
affected_components: app/lib/findependence_app/web.ex plug order (host_check before security_headers); no error handler
findings.impact: No CSP, nosniff or no-store on those responses; bodies are static or empty.
findings.privacy_harm: None.
findings.reproduction: Foreign Host header; a crashing request.
findings.remediation: security_headers first; Plug.ErrorHandler.
findings.regression_test: Headers on 421 and 500.

findings.title: A malformed vault file, or a few crashing requests, stop the local server
attack_prerequisites: T1 edits the file, or a member sends crashing requests
findings.impact: The serve process exits. Availability against T1 is a stated non-goal.
findings.privacy_harm: None.
findings.reproduction: Vault with an unknown atom in a proposal: Store init fails repeatedly; server shuts down.
findings.remediation: Keep the last good vault and report a readable error.
findings.regression_test: A bad file gives an error page, not an exit.

findings.title: The built release's distribution cookie is world-readable
affected_data: the running node and its in-memory keys
attack_prerequisites: a local user on the host, or a copy of the release
findings.impact: Distribution is bound to loopback, so exposure is limited to the host; connections are audited but the audit can then be altered.
findings.privacy_harm: Potentially all signed-in members' data.
findings.reproduction: stat of the built COOKIE file.
findings.remediation: Require RELEASE_COOKIE from a 0600 secret; dedicated OS user; RELEASE_DISTRIBUTION=none unless a console is needed.
findings.regression_test: Release step asserts cookie mode 0600 or less.

findings.title: Hosted sessions have no absolute lifetime and are node-local
affected_data: unwrapped private keys held in memory
attack_prerequisites: a stolen, continuously used session cookie
findings.impact: A session used at least every 15 minutes never ends; with more than one node, a leave or passphrase change would not end sessions elsewhere.
findings.privacy_harm: Longer exposure of a stolen session.
findings.reproduction: Code reading.
findings.remediation: An absolute lifetime (e.g. 12 hours); cluster-wide session store before scaling out.
findings.regression_test: A session older than the limit is refused.

findings.title: Production configuration accepts a default host and an unchecked email-hash key
attack_prerequisites: operator misconfiguration
findings.impact: PHX_HOST falls back to example.com silently; a short EMAIL_HMAC_KEY lets anyone with database access recover addresses by guessing.
findings.privacy_harm: Email addresses recoverable from hashes with a weak key.
findings.reproduction: Config reading.
findings.remediation: Raise without PHX_HOST; decode and require at least 32 bytes of key.
findings.regression_test: Runtime config raises on both.

findings.title: Smaller hardening items
affected_components: /specimen LiveView routed without sign-in in production
client-chosen _form tokens and unbounded form-memory tables
tailwind binary not checksum-pinned; container images not digest-pinned
a second session opened before joining gives 500 on /join
findings.impact: Small extra surface or robustness gaps; none exposes data.
findings.privacy_harm: None.
findings.reproduction: Code reading and headers.
findings.remediation: Gate /specimen behind dev_routes; add Permissions-Policy; issue server-side form tokens with bounded memory; 0700 upload tmpdir; pin binary hashes and image digests.
findings.regression_test: Route and header tests.

findings.title: The hosted operator can read what signed-in members can read
affected_components: hosted/lib/findependence_hosted/sessions.ex (unwrapped private keys in a public ETS table)
attack_prerequisites: operator or console access to the running node
findings.impact: Stated in ARCH-003 and the disclosure; the legal question is open in GATE-016.
findings.privacy_harm: Operator visibility while members are signed in.
findings.reproduction: Design reading.
findings.remediation: Keep the disclosure; audit console access (done); consider client-side keys if the operator must be excluded.
findings.regression_test: n/a
